title: What the Sydney Jazz Club was like
summary: Bull describes the club as a Saturday night dance with a jazz band, a quarterly magazine and older record nights.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: No, no. I still, I have to interrupt you again on another point. What was the jazz club like in Australia? You know, they're different here.

Uh-huh. Yeah, well, the jazz club in Sydney, um, well, it, it started out as, um, so I imagine, as a group of fellows who used to play instruments and got together, and they started, uh, they hired a, a cheap hall in town and they used to play it for Saturday night just for their own enjoyment and then they opened the doors to see if people would come in. Well, um, um, when I first started going down there, they didn't get very many people, they used to get 50 or 100 people a night, on a Saturday night. Um, and that's what it was, it was just like a, really a dance where a jazz band played. But you could become a member of the club and then you'd get, they'd send you the quarterly rag, which is their magazine, you have, I suppose you've had it here, haven't you? No, I don't think I've ever seen it. Well, we'll talk about that afterwards and I'll arrange to have it sent to you every month, every quarter. Um, and you could be a member of the club and then you got in for a couple of bob less next week sort of thing and then they, they used to have record, uh, rhythm club meetings, they call them in those days. This is before my time, I've only heard about this by word of mouth, I've never been to them. They used to have record nights and so and so would have a good record collection and, uh, um, then they'd have a night where all the people would go to his place and they, they used to play. Um, I remember Fred Starkey used to have his, uh, his treasured Jabbo Smiths. You know the Jabbo Smiths rhythm aces things? Yeah. And, uh, they were, they were sort of treasured pieces and you'd go along and, uh, if you became really familiar he'd play you his Jabbo Smith rhythm aces. Anyway, that was before my time. Um, but that's what the jazz club's like, really and still is, a Saturday night dance which has a jazz band playing. That's all. And, uh, consequently you, you get a crowd of, uh, um, well a small percentage of the crowd these days are jazz fans. The rest of them are kids who, uh, like dancing to jazz and like to sort of, you know.
